subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-profile managed-browser proxy config plus per-agent/subagent default browser-profile binding, and what security model should govern proxy credentials, SSRF enforcement, profile selection, inheritance, and concurrency limits?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing surface, but the requested feature defines new public config/API and changes browser egress plus logged-in session isolation semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
options.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for SecretRef-safe proxy auth, explicit proxy/SSRF trust gates, profile authorization, subagent inheritance rules, launch serialization, and resource limits.

options.title: Split proxy and ownership tracks
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60035 own broader proxy egress while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85672 owns browser session inheritance and observability, then narrow this umbrella afterward.

options.title: Document current workarounds
options.body: Decline first-class per-agent/per-profile config for now and document explicit profile, browser.extraArgs, remote CDP, node-host, and external browser-lock style patterns as supported alternatives.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
recommendation.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for SecretRef-safe proxy auth, explicit proxy/SSRF trust gates, profile authorization, subagent inheritance rules, launch serialization, and resource limits.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for browser plugin profile/config/CDP ownership points to steipete, and this choice needs product and security direction for that surface.
